questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely only on your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you are turning.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. You should:

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Move to a different lane if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles merging from an entrance ramp. Move to another lane away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them enter safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume your motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer and smaller lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the posted speed limit and only happen where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following too closely behind you, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse by encouraging them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could skid.
Motorcycle could speed up too fast.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk forward and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Hold the handlebars tighter and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Weaving side to side is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, your motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May increase.
questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases how long it takes to stop. Start slowing down and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: To give space to drivers merging from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Move to the next lane if possible.
Not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if you can.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slower body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly. Slow down by releasing the throttle. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which of these best protects a rider?

options.text: Shoes that don't cover the ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles. Boots should have low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: What should you see when you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for hazards behind you.

questions.question: When riding downhill with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without one?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight, which means you need more braking force. Stopping takes longer on downhill slopes than on flat ground.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, release the throttle and go straight. If you need to brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you know which one it is.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT safe for preventing rider fatigue?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Taking pills or drugs to stay awake.
Limiting how far you ride in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking pills or drugs to stay awake.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks on long trips and don't ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not take artificial stimulants, because you may have a dangerous crash when they wear off.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not protect you from injury.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake. The skid will stop.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: The body gets rid of one alcoholic drink per hour. Someone drank eight drinks four hours ago. How many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the number of drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding?

options.text: Lean the same way the driver leans.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold the seat with their hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way the driver leans.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you through turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid the slippery road.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may miss a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the driver's blind spot. The driver may turn into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your path of escape if danger appears.
